title: Support and resistance: where price pauses
desc: Floors, ceilings and where to put your stop

cards.title: The third visit
cards.situation: This stock bounced off $40 three times this year. Now it’s falling toward $40 again. What often happens?

chart.label: Price bounces off $40 three times and is falling toward it again

options.feedback: It can break, but many traders remember $40 and buy there again.

options.text: Buyers often step in again near $40
options.feedback: Buyers stepped in at $40 before, so many watch it again. That’s [[support|support]].
Trading never stops at a price level. $40 is just where buyers stepped in before, so many watch it again.

cards.work: Bounced near $40 in March, May and July.

cards.title: Floors and ceilings
cards.text: **[[support|Support]]** is a level where buyers stepped in before: a floor. **[[resistance|Resistance]]** is where sellers stepped in: a ceiling.

chart.label: Price swings between support at $40 and resistance at $48

blocks.tip: They’re zones, not exact lines. Price often pokes a little through before turning.

cards.title: When a floor breaks
cards.text: Support at $40 breaks and price falls to $35. Later it climbs back to $40, and stalls there.

chart.label: Support at $40 breaks, price falls to $35, climbs back to $40 and stalls

cards.foot: Broken support often turns into resistance. The buyers who got trapped at $40 sell to get out even.

cards.title: Plan with levels
cards.text: Levels don’t predict. They help you plan: where you’re wrong, and where you might take profit.

blocks.tip: Risk $3 a share to make $7. Decide it before you buy.

cards.title: Place the stop
cards.q: You buy at $41, just above support at $40. Where should your stop-loss go?

options.feedback: Price often dips into a zone before it turns. A stop right on the line gets hit by normal noise.
A little below the whole zone, a normal dip into support won’t stop you out, and you know your risk.
A stop above your entry would sell as soon as you buy. A stop-loss for a buy goes below the price.
Support can break. Without a stop, one bad break can cost far more than $3 a share.

cards.title: Old floor
cards.q: Support at $40 broke and price fell to $35. Now it’s rising back to $40. What might $40 act as now?

options.feedback: Once a floor breaks, it often becomes a ceiling. Sellers wait there.
Broken support often turns into resistance: buyers trapped at $40 sell there to get out even.
$40 still matters: many traders remember it. Once a floor breaks, it often becomes a ceiling.
Price rising into an old floor is no buy signal. Traders trapped at $40 often wait there to sell.

cards.headline: You can find where price might pause.
lines: Support is a floor, resistance a ceiling. Both are zones.
Stops go a little beyond the zone, not on it.
